Both round-1 blocking gaps are now closed with complete telemetry, and H1's remaining weakness is a bounded, non-blocking uncertainty rather than a ranking risk.

What changed since round 1: (1) The H4 discriminator was run. F18/F19 show pricing-engine CPU flat ~40% through the 12:02 bucket and stepping in 12:03–12:04 to a 99–100% plateau that persists to 13:00 (F21), while F20 shows request_rate flat (~583–717, mean 645.7) with NO step at onset, and F23 shows market-data-service throughput and pricing-engine memory flat too. That is the signature of a per-request cost increase (H1), not volume/capacity saturation (H4) — which would require a throughput or traffic-mix step. H4's chain now has an explicit evidence-free first hop and its own supporting set is contradicted by F20/F13/F24/F26/F17. (2) The only shared datastore alternative was closed: F31–F35 show redis-cache CPU/memory/hit-ratio/evictions/clients flat with zero WARN logs, all series missing_points 0 / partial false. With HIST-107 being the only concrete alternative precedent, H2 is contradicted rather than merely unsupported. (3) Temporal order holds where it matters: pricing-engine degrades first (F7 latency step 12:02–12:06; F9 GreeksV2 slow-calc log 12:05:21Z, deadline-exceeded 12:06:41Z), order-service follows ~1 min later at 12:06:10Z with a single timeout signature and no serialization errors (F8). Residual weaknesses I am accepting rather than blocking: the flag's changed_at (12:04:00Z, F24) is ~2 min after the 12:02 latency bucket (F7), and no staged/effective timestamp exists (F25/F29, no historical staging precedent) — but F19/F18 place the CPU step at 12:03–12:04, i.e. coincident with the recorded ramp, and the 12:02 bucket straddles that boundary at 120s resolution. So the "cause before effect" inversion is at most a ~1–2 min bucket-alignment artifact, and the alternative that would exploit it (a 12:02 contemporaneous capacity event) is affirmatively contradicted by flat throughput. The per-call cost jump is still inferred from the flag key/description naming the exact slowed code path (GreeksV2Calculator, F9) plus the CPU step coincidence, not from an A/B measurement — this is the reason for the 0.80 cap, not for another round.
